newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa says dividend growth to continue.
newsitem.headline: Endesa says dividend growth to continue.

text.p: Returns paid to shareholders by Spanish utility Endesa will continue to grow in real terms in the coming years, chairman Rodolfo Martin Villa said on Wednesday.

"Our forecast is that in the next few years the dividend will continue to grow in real terms, which will produce a gradual increase in payout, at present at 44 percent," Martin Villa told shareholders at the annual meeting.

In his address to shareholders, the chairman highlighted the firm's plans to reduce costs by 82.0 billion pesetas by the year 2001. Of this figure, 40.0 billion pesetas correspond to operating costs and the rest to financial costs.
"Not only will personnel costs be reduced but also all areas of management," he said.
Shareholders approved a change in the firm's name, which will cease to be formally Empresa Nacional de Electriciad, S.A. and will become Endesa S.A. ahead of the upcoming privatisation.
The state is due to sell up to 33 percent of Endesa in a privatisation this autumn. State holding company Sepi still owns 57 percent of the utility at present.
Shareholders also approved an increase in the number of board members to 18 from 12, and a total dividend of 180 pesetas per share.
They also gave the go-ahead for a four-for-one share split, although no date for the split to take place was given.
